messages:
alyssa (DevEx PM): Quick sync — proposing Q3 DevEx roadmap focus: SDK parity (Py/Node), 5-min quickstarts, and 2 sample apps (chat + indexer). Need to define launch criteria and scope. Thoughts?

jordan (SDK eng): +1. We should make async streaming parity our highest tech risk. Python async client first, Node streaming next. Also want consistent telemetry hooks in SDKs.

sam (docs): Agree on the priorities. Docs side needs a very small "first run" quickstart (5 steps), plus a longer tutorial for sample apps. Can we target a tiny Next.js + serverless demo for the chat app? Need the API snippets early.

paul (product): Customer asks: enterprise POCs want SSO + VPC deployment examples. Launch metrics we care about: time-to-first-success < 10 minutes, zero install friction for quickstart, and adoption in >=3 pilot customers. If we can't deliver Node streaming immediately, prioritize Python + Next.js for faster wins.

alyssa (DevEx PM): Draft launch criteria proposal (to agree on):
- SDK parity: same surface area for generate/chat/embeddings across languages (may be partial for streaming)
- Quickstart: <5 steps to make a request and see a response
- Sample apps: 1 chat demo (Next.js) + 1 indexer demo (simple Python)
- Docs: short tutorial + full reference + auth examples (API key, token exchange)
- CI: basic e2e smoke test that runs on PRs
- Enterprise: SSO example + brief VPC notes (can be appendix)
- Success metrics: TTF-success < 10m, > 50% reduction in "setup" support tickets in pilot, 3 POC signups in 6 weeks

If scope is tight, we cut Node sample and push streaming parity to phase 2. OK?

jordan (SDK eng): Reality check: Python async client with streaming hooks = ~3 weeks. Node streaming depends on runtime SDK infra and will need ~6 weeks. CI e2e tests add ~1 week after SDK stabilizes. We can phase: Phase 1 = Python async + Next.js demo (server-side calling Python SDK or direct API), Phase 2 = Node streaming + Next.js client streaming.

sam (docs): I can draft the quickstart and tutorial in 2 weeks if SDKs give stable API signatures. Suggest we include the following curl example in quickstarts for immediate copy/paste:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Hello!"}'
```
Keep it minimal. Also will add a troubleshooting section and telemetry hooks doc snippet.

alyssa (DevEx PM): Good. Decisions captured: Phase 1 = Python async SDK + docs + 1 sample app (chat Next.js SSR or serverless) + CI smoke tests + quickstarts. Phase 2 = Node streaming + client-side Next.js streaming + SSO/VPC expanded examples. Action items: Jordan -> update RFC + break into tasks; Sam -> start quickstart draft; Paul -> confirm pilot customers for signups; I'll schedule a follow-up sync in 3 days to firm scope.

jordan (SDK eng): ACK. I'll update the RFC and create issues. Tagging @ci-bot to create tracking issue now.

ci-bot: Created issue RD-4852 in devex/roadmap: "DevEx Q3 Phase 1 - Python async SDK + Next.js chat quickstart".

paul (product): Also add a short cost-estimation snippet and recommended Dedicated settings in the sample app README (we've had customers ask for cost vs latency guidance).

alyssa (DevEx PM): Added to checklist. Thanks everyone — will send updated RFC and task list after Jordan's issues land. Follow-up meeting scheduled: 3 days from now.
